item.title: Real thrash PSV, Arsenal and City stumble, Como go third
item.description: Real thrash PSV, Arsenal and City stumble, Como go third What a night! The first matches of Matchday 5 in the 2026-2027 Champions League league phase took place on Tuesday night. Aside from another defeat for Lens, beaten 3-1 away at Leipzig , the night's main talking point came at the Santiago Bernabeu! Trailing at half-time, Los Blancos completely turned things around against PSV Eindhoven to claim a thumping 5-1 win. Federico Valverde, Jude Bellingham ( who scored the night's standout screamer ), Kylian Mbappé, who bagged a brace, and Vinicius Junior all found the net in the second half. A fifth win in five games takes Madrid provisionally clear at the top of the standings on 15 points, with PSG still to face AS Roma tomorrow. Behind them, the two main Premier League title rivals also dropped points at home. Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund, while Manchester City had to settle for a 2-2 draw against Napoli. City even had to come from behind twice to salvage a point! Another big winner on the night was Como! The Italian club continued their incredible run with a 1-0 victory over AEK Athens. With 12 points, they provisionally move into third place in the league phase standings, just ahead of Real Betis, who also have 12 points after their 2-0 win away at Slovan Bratislava. item.title: Walter Clayton Jr. Confidence Makes Him A Dallas Mavericks Staple
item.description: Peter Creveling-Imagn Images Walter Clayton Jr. has become a key piece for the Dallas Mavericks because he refuses to back down. He went from being waived to becoming a key floor general behind Kyrie Irving. The Smoking Cuban reported that his confidence drives his rapid rise in Dusty May’s rotation. In nine of the last 11 games, Clayton logged a minimum of 20 minutes. Against the Utah Jazz on Sunday night, he recorded three assists and nine points in a close victory. Since the February trade, this was his first away matchup versus Utah. Jazz Coach Will Hardy Admits Clayton Is a Pain Utah head coach Will Hardy spoke about Clayton’s mindset before the game on November 22. Hardy’s comments show why Dallas fans should feel good about his future. He told reporters, “Walt was a pain in the (expletive), in a great way.” Hardy added that he has so much respect for Clayton because he is a self-made guy. The player was not highly touted coming out of high school but fought his way up. Fearlessly inserting himself into the action, he carries a large chip on his shoulder. This physical style fits the Mavericks perfectly. Defense and Rebounding Drive the Rise One of the most impressive parts of Clayton’s game is his defense. He competes hard on that end and crashes the glass with great effort. Clayton relentlessly chases rebounds and has buckled down after a rough start to his play earlier this season. There is no player he thinks he cannot guard. This same mentality shows up on offense where he plays with no fear. He hangs in the air on drives and sprays the ball out with accurate wrap-around passes. He lets threes fly from anywhere beyond the arc. The foundation he laid as a big-time shot-maker at Florida is clear for everyone to see. The Florida Gators’ 2025 senior National Championship leader, who averaged 18.3 points per game, may not resemble the current Clayton. Yet the crafty playmaker is showing his value in Dallas. The Jazz traded him away less than a year ago, and now they are rethinking that move. Hardy Praises the Competitive Motor Jazz head coach Will Hardy said Clayton is fearless and his competitive motor is really high. He noted that he has a lot of respect for Walt and how he goes about it.

The Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11, and it was a huge win to keep pace in the AFC West with the Kansas City Chiefs right in line with them. Dobbins didn't gain any yards on one rush, and his role has significantly diminished. For Week 12 against the Pittsburgh Steelers for the NFL's Black Friday Game, Dobbins isn't going to be involved at all. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo is reporting that Dobbins has been suspended by the Broncos, but the exact reason isn't known. Broncos suspend J.K. Dobbins for Week 12 for unknown reason "Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins is suspended for this week's game against the Steelers for conduct detrimental to the team, per HC Sean Payton, who did not provide further details," Garafolo reports. On Tuesday afternoon, the Broncos made the surprise decision to suspend Dobbins for one week due to "conduct detrimental to the team." But what exactly did Dobbins do that led to this suspension? It's not known why this suspension was put on Dobbins, but it is fair to wonder if it has to do with his workload decreasing. Through the first six weeks of the NFL season, Dobbins ran the ball 8, 10, 17, 11, 18, and 17 times. Gakpo sat out the 4-0 Premier League demolition of Manchester United on Sunday with a calf injury picked up during international duty with the Netherlands last week, while Gravenberch has been sidelined for nearly a month battling a heel issue. Both players will miss the UEFA Champions League match against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, with Liverpool looking to edge closer to securing automatic passage to the knockout stages. -Credit:DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images Furthermore, both Gakpo and Gravenberch look almost certain to sit out Sunday's Premier League visit to Everton. "With Cody, it's a soleus (calf) injury," said Iraola, according to the Liverpool Echo . "It's a muscle injury. It's not big, but we expected that he was out. He's going to be out even for the weekend. It's more predictable. "With Ryan, it's difficult to say. He is having pain. These things in the fascia (heel) are difficult to solve. Sometimes he is managing the pain but for now he is not in a good place. "Let's see if we can find ways of solving the problem a little bit but these injuries are not easy to go, normally." item.title: ARCA Schedules Drop: East And West Sets 2027 Race Dates
item.description: David Leong-Imagn Images The ARCA Menards Series has locked in its 2027 calendar, setting the stage for a busy year of stock car racing. The East division will run eight events, while the West division faces a grueling thirteen-race slate. Speedway Media reported the full details on Tuesday, November 24, giving teams time to plan their travel and budgets. The East season kicks off on March 27 at the historic Hickory Motor Speedway. That track hosted a near-capacity crowd last year, proving that short tracks still draw massive interest. The series then heads south to Bradenton, Florida, for a new stop at Cleetus McFarland’s Freedom Factory on April 17. Daily Downforce noted this will be the first time the East series races at the three-eighths-mile track. It is a bold move that mixes traditional oval racing with the unique culture of McFarland’s venue. East Series Takes on New Challenges After the Florida stop, the East tour returns to familiar grounds with races at Nashville Fairgrounds on May 1 and Toledo Speedway on May 15. The summer stretch includes a trip to Iowa Speedway on July 2, followed by back-to-back weekends in the Midwest. Flat Rock Speedway hosts a race on July 17, and Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park follows on July 23. The season wraps up at World Wide Technology Raceway on August 20, just outside of St. Louis. ARCA President Ron Drager told reporters, “We’ve seen some real excitement around the ARCA Menards Series East the last couple of seasons.” He pointed to the big event feel at Hickory as a key reason to keep the momentum going. West Division Faces a Longer Grind The West division has a much heavier workload with thirteen races scheduled. The opener returns to Phoenix Raceway on March 12, setting the tone for a long campaign. Phoenix and Kern Raceway are the only tracks scheduled to host the series twice. The season finale takes place at Kern on October 30, marking the second straight year the West ends there. Drager continued his comments on the West slate, stating, “We’re just as enthused with the momentum in the ARCA Menards Series West.” He credited the strong car counts from recent years for creating terrific racing that keeps fans interested. New stops include Stateline Speedway and Meridian Speedway in Idaho, which add fresh challenges for drivers. The series aims to carry its current success forward into the 2027 season. While the East focuses on a tight eight-race schedule, the West drivers must manage a thirteen-race grind that tests their endurance. The mix of historic tracks and new venues gives the series a balanced appeal for both old-school fans and new viewers. Nitro Motorsports is already preparing for the season by signing George Phillips as a full-time driver for the East campaign. The team will field the No. 15 car driven by a North Carolina native aged 18. Phillips joins a roster that includes Jake Bollman, Kasey Kleyn, and Wesley Slimp for national campaigns. item.title: Panthers Need Four Wins To Lock NFC South Title
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Carolina Panthers beat the Baltimore Ravens 35-33 on Sunday night at Bank of America Stadium. This win puts the team back at .500 for the season. Every other team in the division sits at 3-7 right now. That gap looks big, but the road ahead is full of traps. The Panthers have seven games left on their schedule. Four of those are against teams outside the division. The other three are against division rivals who are desperate to catch up. A win against Tampa Bay on Monday night changes the whole math for the season. Per Cat Scratch Reader , the Panthers might only need three wins to clinch the division title if they beat the Buccaneers. That game happens at Raymond James Stadium. It is a tough spot to play. The Buccaneers have an easier schedule than Carolina does. They only face one team with a winning record for the rest of the year. That opponent is the Rams in Week 17. If the Panthers lose on Monday, the pressure will mount fast. The tiebreaker rules would then favor Tampa Bay. The Panthers would need to create distance quickly to stay safe. The Four Win Safety Net Most fans and analysts think four wins are the magic number to lock up the playoff spot. This is a high bar for a team with a mixed record. The remaining non-division games are the biggest test. The Panthers play the Vikings on the road and the Steelers away. They also host the Bengals and the Seahawks. With a 6-4 record, the Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions. The other three teams are in the playoffs, while the Seahawks are out of the postseason picture. Beating any of these teams is a hard task. Division games are the key to the title race. The Panthers play one game against each of the other NFC South teams. The Saints can make up ground on Tampa Bay in their upcoming game against the Cardinals. If the Panthers sweep the division, it creates the most distance possible. To overtake Carolina straight up, someone would have to win out. That is a very tall order for the Saints or the Falcons. The math favors Carolina if they stay healthy. Monday Night Is The Tipping Point The game on Monday, Nov. 30 is the most important one left on the schedule. It starts at 8:15 p.m. ET. The Panthers travel to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers. A win here sets the tone for the final stretch. A loss forces the team to win more games than planned to stay ahead. If the Panthers lose that game, they will face pressure to build a lead over Tampa, which has a simpler schedule and a tiebreaker advantage. For that to happen, the easiest way is for the Panthers to sweep the division.

item.title: From College Tennis to the PPL: Guille Jiménez Cagigas on Growing Padel in America
item.description: During my time writing about the U.S. padel scene, I’ve run into a ton of folks who came to this country to play college tennis and who are now driving the growth of padel here. The latest of these fellows is Guillermo “Guille” Jiménez Cagigas. After a distinguished junior tennis career in Spain, Guille played five seasons of tennis at Longwood University in Virginia, where he rose to the number one singles spot in his final season. He transitioned to padel and is currently ranked No. 8 in the 2026 USA Padel Circuit standings. In addition to playing for the Smash and elsewhere, he co-founded the padel performance training company PadelEdge. As a former member of USA Padel’s Junior Development Committee (2024), he has a unique vantage point on the growth and expansion of padel, especially junior padel, in this country. Guille was in Las Vegas last week to represent the hometown Las Vegas Smash in the PPL’s regular-season finale at Dolby Live. It was a tough week. He and partner Agustín Torre got routined in both of their matches, and the Smash came up a point short of qualifying for the PPL Finals next week in Miami. Luckily, I sat down with him before the start of the event, and he was in a fine mood. item.description: NICEVILLE, Fla. — Kennedy Blair’s career-best scoring game was not enough to help the Michigan State women’s basketball team capture the title at the Emerald Coast Classic. item.title: Tiger Woods’ Sun Day Red dealt setback in trademark fight over leaping tiger logo
item.description: A divided federal appeals court on Tuesday ordered the dismissal of a trademark lawsuit by Tiger Woods' golf apparel company, which sought approval to use its "leaping tiger" logo after another company with a similar logo objected. Reversing a lower court ruling, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals in Pasadena, California, said courts in that state lacked jurisdiction to consider claims by Woods' Sun Day Red against Tigeraire, a Louisiana company that makes cooling fans attachable to athletes' headgear. The 2-1 majority said this was because Tigeraire, which is affiliated with the Louisiana State University Tigers, had no physical presence in California and did little business there. More: What your golf fit says about you: Sun Day Red Tuesday's decision does not affect Tigeraire's trademark infringement lawsuit against Sunday Red, which has been on hold. Lawyers for both companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Sunday Red, based in San Clemente, California, is part of TaylorMade Golf, which is a subsidiary of South Korean private equity firm Centroid Investment Partners. Sun Day Red, as Woods' brand is known, launched in February 2024, paying homage to Woods' wearing red on Sunday during golf tournaments. Its logo contains 15 stripes, one for each of Woods' major championship titles. Shortly after Sun Day Red's launch, Tigeraire, which launched in 2020, sent a cease-and-desist letter that said the competing logos were confusing consumers. Settlement talks failed, prompting the dueling lawsuits. Sunday Red's lawsuit sought a declaration it did nothing wrong, and accused Tigeraire of seeking an "unwarranted financial windfall from a larger and more successful brand." A federal judge refused to dismiss the case, and Tigeraire appealed. Writing for Tuesday's majority, Circuit Judge Morgan Christen called Tigeraire's sales in California "trivial," totaling just 80 products over eight months and including only one item of apparel, a T-shirt. She also called the cease-and-desist letter a "garden-variety" attempt to begin settlement talks, which did not support asserting jurisdiction. Circuit Judge Milan Smith dissented. He said the majority was too quick to dismiss Sunday Red's claim it could face irreparable harm if forced to pull products from stores and rebrand itself while Tigeraire asserted its trademark rights. Woods, 50, launched Sun Day Red after his 27-year partnership with Nike NKE.N ended. item.description: NFL insider reveals if teams called Browns about a Shedeur Sanders trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns are locked into Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback going forward for the rest of the season, and for good reason. He's been playing great this year and is more than deserving of keeping the starting job. But that has meant Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and, to a lesser degree, Taylen Green won't be seeing the field unless Watson is out. That, naturally, led to questions about whether Sanders would be drawing trade interest at the deadline or not. Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported two weeks after the NFL trade deadline that the Browns did not field any calls about Sanders or Gabriel at the trade deadline, showing that teams didn't have much interest in either this season. Browns didn't get any trade calls on Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel "The Browns received no trade calls on backup quarterbacks Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel at or before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, league sources told Cleveland.com," Cabot reported. This report from Cabot is very interesting, as there were some quarterback-needy teams at the NFL trade deadline, and yet none of them called the Browns about a potential trade. Cleveland didn't field any trade offers for Sanders or Gabriel this year, even though both would seem to have been readily available had a team made a competitive offer. Both are firmly behind Watson on the depth chart, and with Green as a developmental option, the Browns don't really need four quarterbacks. So, a trade for one of Sanders or Gabriel would've made sense. MORE : Updated 2027 NFL Draft order: What Jets win over Chargers in Week 11 means for No. 1 pick race And yet, no team made an offer. Whether it was due to a lack of interest in both, or simply that the Browns made it clear they didn't want to trade either, no teams made an effort to call; the Browns never received an offer, let alone a trade call on either QB. Cleveland was looking to add at the NFL trade deadline, so it's not a total surprise they weren't in a selling market. But, considering the QB of the future in Cleveland is likely not on the roster right now, a trade of either QB would make sense. This upcoming offseason, Sanders and/or Gabriel could be on the move. Neither has much of a future with the Browns, so it wouldn't be shocking if they were traded in 2027. But for now, no NFL team seemingly has interest in Sanders or Gabriel, as the Browns didn't get any trade calls about either QB leading up to the November 10 NFL trade deadline. item.title: Trevor Etienne Forces Panthers To Rethink Chuba Hubbard’s Role
item.description: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Carolina Panthers fans watching the 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens saw a clear shift in the backfield. Trevor Etienne is no longer just a special teams player or a depth option waiting for an injury. Head coach Dave Canales is responding to the young runner’s request for more touches as the team seeks any edge to stay competitive in the NFC South. In the last two games, Chuba Hubbard has carried the load as the workhorse with 27 carries each. His physical style has been vital, but the team cannot rely on him alone for the rest of the season. Etienne showed he can handle the pressure when he got the chance. Showing much improved conviction, he exploited seams for decent gains and flashed real promise. Hard work by the runner aims to build trust in his capacity to deliver, as noted by the coach. A Coach’s Shift in Strategy Dave Canales made his stance clear after the game. He wants to reward the player who is proving his worth through action. “Trevor’s showing us he wants the ball. Trevor wants to be a factor, and he wants to help his team. So, we’ll look for more opportunities to get him involved,” Canales said, according to Cat Crave . This quote signals a major change in how the Panthers will use their running backs. The timing matters. Jonathon Brooks has not been activated yet, and there is no telling when that will happen. With Brooks out, the Panthers need to find a way to keep Hubbard fresh without slowing down the offense. Etienne’s growing confidence and his ability to contribute on special teams make him the perfect solution. Etienne is capitalizing on the present opportunity, even though the 2024 second-round pick could face a delayed return. Competition Breeds Success Etienne capitalizing on the present opportunity creates a problem for the Panthers, but it is a good one. As a rookie, Etienne was viewed as nothing more than a kick returner. Now, the Georgia product is starting to shake things up regarding the running back dynamic. Jonathon Brooks has not put anything on tape since entering the league that surpasses Etienne’s flashes in Week 11. That is a bold statement, but the numbers and the tape back it up. The Panthers have an interesting dynamic brewing behind Hubbard. They have not given up on Brooks, but they cannot wait forever for him to be ready. Fans will monitor the timing of Brooks’ return closely, especially since he lacks special-teams impact. At long last, Etienne has his foot in the door for now. The Panthers face their next challenge on Monday, Nov. 30, at 8:15 p.m. ET, when they travel to Raymond James Stadium to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
